response.title: Deep Portfolio Management A Deep Reinforcement Learning Framework for the Financial Portfolio Management Problem
response.horizon: one 30-minute trading period between portfolio redistributions
response.label_definition: No supervised label is defined; the reinforcement learning reward for action wt over the next period is the logarithmic rate of return rt+1 = ln(mu_t+1 * yt+1 · wt).
data_requirements: Use Poloniex cryptocurrency price data accessed through Poloniex official API.
For Back-Test 1, train on data from 2014-11-01 00:00 UTC to 2016-09-07 04:00 UTC.
Evaluate Back-Test 1 from 2016-09-07 04:00 UTC to 2016-10-28 08:00 UTC.
Use closing prices for cross-validation and back-tests.
Use highest, lowest, and closing prices in the periods for training.
Preselect 12 assets total including cash and Bitcoin using trading volumes over the last 30 days before the back-test.
feature_groups: historical price matrix window with 50 trading periods
closing prices for training, cross-validation, and back-tests
previous portfolio weights via Portfolio-Vector Memory
model_families: EIIE CNN reinforcement learning policy network
response.training_protocol: For the selected Back-Test 1 experiment, use the EIIE CNN policy network. Pre-train on the Back-Test 1 training set for 2 × 10^6 total steps with mini-batch size 50, input window size 50, Adam learning rate 3 × 10^-5, L2 regularization coefficient 10^-8, and online stochastic batch learning with 30 rolling steps per period during cross-validation and back-tests. Epoch count, random seed, exact CNN layer specification, and stopping rule are unknown from the supplied context.
response.evaluation_protocol: Chronological back-test on Poloniex with Back-Test 1 interval 2016-09-07 04:00 UTC to 2016-10-28 08:00 UTC, using 30-minute periods and closing prices. Hyperparameters are selected using the separate cross-validation interval 2016-05-07 04:00 UTC to 2016-06-27 08:00 UTC. The paper describes this as a fixed historical back-test, not a rolling or walk-forward holdout.
metrics: final Accumulated Portfolio Value (fAPV) in units of initial portfolio amount pf/p0
response.preprocessing_protocol: Missing historical coin data appearing as NANs in the training set are replaced with flat fake price movements using 0 decay rate. The supplied context does not specify normalization details or whether any statistics are fit on training data only.
strict_requirements: Use the CNN EIIE model, not the bRNN or LSTM EIIE rows.
Use the Back-Test 1 chronological train and test ranges exactly.
Use 12 preselected assets including cash and Bitcoin.
Do not infer exact CNN EIIE MDD, fAPV, or SR values from the supplied context because the numeric row is not visible.
unknowns: Exact Back-Test 1 CNN EIIE MDD, fAPV, and SR values are not present in the supplied context.

evidence_spans.quote: Deep Portfolio Management A Deep Reinforcement Learning Framework for the Financial Portfolio Management Problem
This paper presents a ﬁnancial-model- free Reinforcement Learn- ing framework to provide a deep machine learning solution to the port folio management problem.
examined in three back-test experiments with a trading period of 30 minutes in a cryptocurrency mar- ket.
number of assets 12 Total number of preselected assets (including the cash, Bitcoin). (Section 3.1)
Prices are accessed in periods of 30 minut es.
trading period (second) 1800 Time interval between two portfolio redistributions. (Section 2.1)

At the end of Period t + 1, the logarithmic rate of return for the period due to decis ion wt can be calculated with the additional information from the price change vecto r yt+1, using Equation (10), rt+1 = ln( µ t+1yt+1 · wt). In the language of RL, rt+1 is the immediate reward to the portfolio management agent for its action wt under environment condition Xt.
All price data is accesse d with Poloniex’s oﬃcial Application Programming Interface (API)
Closing prices are used for cross validation and back-tests, while highest, lo west, and closing prices in the periods are used for training.
window size 50 Number of the columns (number of the trading periods) in each input price matrix. (Section 3.2)
The framework is real- ized in three instants in this work with a Convolutional Neural Networ k (CNN), a basic Re- current Neural Network (RNN), and a Long Short-Term Memory ( LSTM).
total steps 2 × 106 Total number of steps for pre-training in the training set.
batch size 50 Size of mini-batch during training. (Section 3.1)
learning rate 3 × 10−5 Parameter α (i.e. the step size) of the Adam optimization (Kingma and Ba, 2014).
A cross validation set is used f or determination of the hyper- parameters, whose range is also listed.
The performance metrics are Maximum Drawdown (MDD), the ﬁnal Accumulated Po rtfolio Value (fAPV) in the unit of initial portfolio amount ( pf /p 0), and the Sharpe ratio (SR).
In term of fAPV or SR, the best performing algorithm in Back-Tes t 1 and 2 is the CNN EIIE whose ﬁnal wealth is more than twice of the runner-up in the ﬁr st experiment.
Although with a high commission rate of 0. 25% in the back- tests, the framework is able to achieve at least 4-fold returns in 50 days.
Data po ints before the existence of a coin are marked as Not A Numbers (NANs) from the exchange. NANs onl y appeared in the training set
in this current work, ﬂat fake price-movements (0 decay rate s) are used to ﬁll the missing data points.

batch size 50 Size of mini-batch during training. (Section 3.1) window size 50 Number of the columns (number of the trading periods) in each input price matrix. (Section 3.2) number of assets 12 Total number of preselected assets (including the cash, Bitcoin). (Section 3.1) trading period (second) 1800 Time interval between two portfolio redistributions.
regularization coeﬃcient 10−8 The L2 regularization coeﬃcient applied to network training. learning rate 3 × 10−5 Parameter α (i.e. the step size) of the Adam optimization (Kingma and Ba, 2014).

commission rate 0. 25% Rate of commission fee applied to each transaction. (Section 2.3) rolling steps 30 Number of online training steps for each period during cross-validation and back-tests. sample bias 5 × 10−5 Parameter of geometric distribution when selecting online training sample batches.

The best perform ance in each column is highlighted with boldface. All three EIIEs signiﬁcantly outperform all other algorithms in the fAPV and SR columns, showing the proﬁtabil ity and reliability of the EIIE machine-learning solution to the portfolio mana gement problem.
